**Review date:** YYYY-MM-DD (Europe/Copenhagen)  
**Participants:** Names of people at the review

The PL facilitates this 15-minute review. Count work items by the rules in the [glossary](/MTGO/architecture/glossary/). An ISO week runs Monday to Sunday in Europe/Copenhagen. Record the board observation time so the WIP count can be checked later. Use “Not available” and explain missing data; do not substitute a guess.

## Flow metrics

| Metric                                      | This week (YYYY-wNN) | Last week (YYYY-wNN) |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------: | -------------------: |
| Throughput (work items closed as completed) |                      |                      |
| Average cycle time (calendar days)          |                      |                      |
| WIP at the review                           |                      |                      |
| WIP limit breaches (if history exists)      |                      |                      |

**Sources and counting:** Link to the board or the issues counted. For cycle time, subtract the project start date from the closing date in Copenhagen calendar dates. Same-day work contributes 0 to the average and can be described as “< 1 day”. Exclude work items closed as not planned, parent issues, and closed work items without a start date from the cycle-time average. Throughput still includes completed work items with a missing start date. Say how many completed work items have a usable start date. For past WIP or breaches, cite status history; if it is unavailable, write “Not available”.

## Old or blocked work items

| Work item           | Status and age at review | Blocker or reason to watch | Next action and owner |
| ------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------------- | --------------------- |
| None, or issue link |                          |                            |                       |

Use the aging rule currently agreed by the team. Include blocked work even if it is not old. Note the observation time.

## What the data showed and what the team experienced

- **Data:** What changed or stood out? Cite the work items behind the number.
- **Team experience:** What did contributors observe during the work?

## Improvement experiment for next week

- **Change:** One concrete change to the way of working.
- **Expected effect:** What should improve?
- **How we will check it:** Which observation or metric, and when?
- **Owner:** Who will make sure it happens?

## Follow-up on last week's experiment

- **What we did:** State “First review; no earlier experiment” if applicable.
- **What the data and observations showed:**
- **Decision:** Continue, adjust, or stop; give the reason.
